definitions.gloss: boasting; bragging; self-promotional claims; sales pitch
definitions.explanation: Self-promoting talk or written claims about how good something is. Originally referred to the description of a medicine's efficacy on its packaging, and by extension came to mean exaggerated claims or boasting in general. Often used dismissively.

examples.japanese: {能書|のうが}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{早|はや}く→早い：00514_hayai⟧⟦やれ→やる：02980_yaru⟧。
examples.english: Enough talk — just get on with it.

examples.japanese: {能書|のうが}き⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦{並|なら}べて→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{信用|しんよう}されない→信用する：25371_shinyousuru⟧。
examples.english: Nobody will trust you if all you do is boast.

examples.japanese: ⟦{商品|しょうひん}→商品：01436_shouhin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{能書|のうが}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}んで→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{効果|こうか}→効果：02726_kouka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{分|わ}からない→分かる：00463_wakaru⟧。
examples.english: Even if you read the product claims, you can't tell if it actually works.

notes:
Originally referred to the printed description of a medicine's ingredients and efficacy ({能書|のうが}き = list of capabilities/effects). Over time, the meaning shifted to 'self-promotional talk' or 'boasting,' with a dismissive or skeptical nuance. Almost always used negatively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {能書|のうが}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{並|なら}べる→並べる：01091_naraberu⟧: to rattle off claims; to boast
- {能書|のうが}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{垂|た}れる→垂れる：10075_tareru⟧: to spout off boasts (blunt/rough)
- {能書|のうが}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧: enough with the talk (dismissive)
- {能書|のうが}き⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧: nothing but boasting

USAGE:
The phrase {能書|のうが}き⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧ is a common way to tell someone to stop talking and start doing. The word carries an inherently skeptical tone — the speaker implies the claims are exaggerated or empty.

ETYMOLOGY:
From {能書|のうしょ} (a document listing the properties and efficacy of medicine) + き (a suffix). The original neutral meaning of 'product description' has largely given way to the negative sense of 'empty boasting.'
